ledger.contains: Vanuatu Ombudsman public report (13 Mar 1998, reissued 18 Mar 1998) on the improper issue since 1993 of diplomatic and official passports to foreign nationals given sham posts as honorary consuls, trade commissioners and advisers: summary counts (about 30 diplomatic and 40 official passports; 70 in all, 64 without an acceptance letter; 3 missing; appointees by country of posting and by appointing minister), Tables 1-2 listing each passport and holder, the law (Cap 179: no fee for these passports; five-year validity), the evidence of payments to ministers (a US$5,000 bank deposit, US$60,000 in cash, US$30,000 in election contributions, a US$15,000 cheque, and Prime Minister Korman's fax requesting US$5,000-10,000 contributions from appointees), the replies, findings and recommendations. Earlier passes recorded 5 counts and 2 events. This pass added 27 numbers: 14 alleged, requested or promised payments to ministers (irregular_payments_alleged; payers, who are private individuals, are not named), 2 missing-passport counts and 11 appointee counts (new indicator improper_passport_appointments); 3 rules (no fee for diplomatic/official passports, their five-year validity, and the 10-year ordinary naturalisation residence as a context row); 2 events (enquiry began September 1997; minister took over issuing in November 1997). Deliberately not recorded: the per-passport rows of Tables 1-2, because each row identifies a private individual (name, passport number, nationality); no figure there is in scope apart from the counts the report summarises.

Committee report (33 pp., January 2026) with the amended text of the Andorran bill on continuity and consolidation of sustainable-growth measures (enacted as Llei 2/2026, whose BOPA text is not stored): list of amendments and votes; immigration-law changes (seasonal and origin-hiring permits, self-employment residence with a EUR 50,000 non-refundable payment, new art. 96 for residence without gainful activity, sanctions for simulated residence), housing law, commerce and foreign real-estate investment tax changes. Out of scope and not recorded: the self-employment route (it requires running a business; decision 15), seasonal and hiring permits, housing, commerce and the foreign real-estate investment tax (not tied to the residence route), and the committee's amendment counts. Earlier pass: one context event. This pass added 10 rules for residence without gainful activity (EUR 1,000,000; EUR 400,000 via the Housing Fund; more than EUR 800,000 per property; 36-month cap on financial instruments; EUR 50,000 and EUR 12,000 non-refundable payments; 6-month deadline and 6-month extension; EUR 3,000-6,000 sanction and up to double the unpaid amount for evading the payments), all marked in notes as the bill's proposed rules (status: proposed) because this bill text is the only stored statement of them, and 1 context event (transitional provision). Replace or confirm them from the BOPA text of Llei 2/2026 once stored.

Addis Fortune article (26 Apr 2026) on Ethiopia's new Golden Visa and property-linked residence: the USD 150,000 property route and five-year residential ID (revoked if the property is sold), the USD 5 million Golden Visa with a USD 10,000 fee for 10 years and renewal fees, the revised ICS fee regulation (21 fee areas; investment visa fees by duration; five-year permanent residence permit USD 3,000; expedited processing USD 4,000-4,500), ICS revenue (31.2 billion Br in three quarters), passports issued, border enforcement and FDI figures. Earlier pass: 5 rules and 1 event. This pass added 7 rules: Golden Visa renewal fees (USD 10,000 after 10 years; USD 12,500 immediate) and the five investment-visa fees by duration (USD 60 to 4,000) as context rows, since the article does not say what qualifies for that visa. Out of scope and not recorded: the permanent residence permit fee and expedited-processing fees (general immigration services, not tied to the investor routes), ICS revenue and passport counts (general immigration agency figures), border enforcement and FDI figures.

Guatemala Migration Code (Decreto 44-2016, approved 20 Sep 2016, sanctioned 12 Oct 2016; in force 60 days after publication): rights of migrants (including property and investment), entry categories, temporary residence categories with maximum periods (investors up to five years, art. 75(d)), extensions at the Institute's discretion (art. 76), permanent residence criteria (art. 78), the migration institutions, refugee procedure, fines for migrants and carriers (Q200, Q15 a day, Q2,000, Q5,000; US$10,000 for carriers), passports and transitional provisions. Earlier pass: art. 75(d) five-year investor permit and the sanction-date event. This pass added 1 rule: permanent residence after five or more years of temporary residence (art. 78(a)), which applies to investors. Out of scope and not recorded: other residence categories, the rentista/pensionado category (income-based; decision 15), fines for migrants and carriers, institutional and refugee provisions and passport validity (general immigration rules not specific to the investor route). The Code contains no naturalisation rules and no fee amounts (fees left to regulations, art. 79).

Guatemala's residence regulation (Acuerdo IGM-016-2025, signed 21 May 2025, approved by AMN-05-2025): general rules for temporary and permanent residence, requirements by category (migrant workers with income tests of US$2,000/3,000 a month, students, artists, investors with US$100,000 (art. 17-18), researchers, clergy, refugees), permanent residence routes (five years' temporary residence, marriage, family, Central Americans, rentistas and pensioners with US$1,250 a month plus US$300 per dependant), cancellation, revocation, registration, rights and obligations, absences, document rules, repeal of IGM-092-2022. Earlier pass: investor amount, residence periods, five-year permanent residence and the signing event. This pass added 10 general rules that apply to investor residents (minimum one-year permit; 30-day renewal deadline and window; two-year police-certificate period; loss of residence after more than one year's unauthorised absence; six-month document age; 30-day registration and cure deadlines; 90-day visa while pending; archiving after six months' inactivity) and 1 event (repeal of the 2022 regulation). Checked and out of scope: the rentista/pensionado category (it rests on a monthly income from pensions, deposits or investments abroad, with no investment in Guatemala; decision 15) and the migrant-worker income tests. Investor dependants follow the migrant-worker rules, which state no ages or amounts.

Isle of Man Immigration Rules consolidated to December 2009 (199 pp.): general provisions, all entry categories, the points-based system (Tier 1 General, Entrepreneur, Investor; Tiers 2, 4, 5), family and dependant routes, deportation, and Appendices A-F. In scope: the Tier 1 (Investor) route (paras 245O-245U; Appendix A paras 42-50, Tables 7-8), points-based dependants as they apply to investors (paras 319A-319J) and the former investor category (paras 224-231; Appendix F as at 1 Dec 2009). Earlier pass: the Table 7 GBP 1 million entry threshold and a context event. This pass added 22 rules: the Table 7 alternative (assets over GBP 2 million plus GBP 1 million loaned), the Table 8 extension amounts (GBP 1 million, GBP 2 million assets, GBP 750,000 invested within 3 months), entry clearance 3 years, leave to remain 2 or 3 years, settlement after 5 years with language exemptions under 18 and 65+, the 12-month sponsor rule, dependants (children under 18, partners 2 years together), and the former investor category (GBP 1 million / GBP 2 million assets, GBP 750,000 incl. one-year deposits, leave up to 2 years, extensions up to 3, settlement after 5 years). Out of scope and not recorded: the other categories and general rules (not specific to the investor route); maintenance-fund amounts (investors are exempt).

Isle of Man Statement of Changes in Immigration Rules SD 2014/0344 (laid 9 Dec 2014, effective 10 Nov 2014; 28 pp.): Tier 1 (General) and Entrepreneur changes, Tier 1 (Investor) changes (source-of-funds tests, GBP 2 million threshold, new Tables 7, 8A, 8B, 9A, 9B, curtailment amounts, qualifying-investment and maintenance rules), private-life and deportation rules (Article 8), and the English-test list (Appendix O). Earlier pass: the GBP 2 million threshold and the price-change event. This pass added 24 Tier 1 (Investor) rules: Table 8A (GBP 2 million invested; 3-month deadline; 12-month prior-investment window), transitional Table 8B (GBP 1 million / GBP 2 million assets / GBP 750,000 / GBP 1,000,000), the curtailment amount, Table 9A (GBP 10 million / GBP 5 million for 2- and 3-year settlement; 2, 3 and 5 years; 180 days' absence limit), transitional Table 9B (GBP 10 / 20 / 5 / 10 million, GBP 1,000,000, 75% in companies), maintenance market values (GBP 750,000 / 3,750,000 / 7,500,000) and the 90-day holding rule. Out of scope and not recorded: the Tier 1 (General) and Entrepreneur changes, Article 8 private-life and deportation rules, and the English-test list (not the investor route).

Archived Isle of Man Immigration Rules in effect 14-22 February 2022 (918 pp.), the last version open to new Tier 1 (Investor) applicants: general provisions, all entry categories, the points-based system, family routes (Part 8 and Appendix FM), deportation and appendices. In scope: Tier 1 (Investor) paras 245E-245EF, Appendix A paras 54-65-SD (Tables 7, 8A, 8B, 9A, 9B; source-of-money, qualifying-investment and maintenance notes incl. para 65 exclusions), and points-based dependants as they apply to investors (paras 319A-319J). Earlier pass: Table 7 GBP 2 million and the Table 9A 5-year settlement period. This pass added 39 rules: Tables 8A/8B (GBP 2 million; GBP 1 million / 2 million assets / 750,000 / 1,000,000; 3-month deadline; 12-month window), curtailment amount, Table 9A (GBP 10 / 5 million; 2 and 3 years; 180 days' absence), Table 9B (GBP 10 / 20 / 5 / 10 million; GBP 1,000,000; 75%), maintenance values (GBP 750,000 / 3,750,000 / 7,500,000), 90-day holding rules, six-month reinvestment, minimum age 18, 28-day overstay disregard, entry clearance 3 years 4 months, leave to remain 2 or 3 years, criminal-record rules (12 months in 10 years; 28 days), and dependants (children under 18; partners 2 years together, 5 years to settle, 180 days' absence, 3 years' leave). Para 65 restrictions (no offshore, pooled, property or deposit investments) have no numbers and are described in notes of earlier rows. Out of scope and not recorded: other categories and general rules, Appendix KoLL language exemptions (general settlement rule for all routes).

Isle of Man Immigration Rules in effect from 23 February 2022 (915 pp.): general provisions, all entry categories, points-based system, family routes, deportation and appendices. In scope: Tier 1 (Investor) paras 245E-245EF (closure statement; extension and settlement rules for existing investors with deadlines of 23 Feb 2026 and 23 Feb 2028), Appendix A paras 54-65-SD (Tables 8A, 8B, 9A, 9B and notes; Table 7 omitted) and points-based dependants (paras 319A-319J). Earlier pass: the closure event. This pass added 33 rules restating the extension and settlement rules for existing investors (Tables 8A/8B, curtailment, Tables 9A/9B incl. 2, 3 and 5 years, 180 days' absence, maintenance values, 90-day and six-month rules, minimum age 18, 28-day overstay disregard, dependants) plus the new 2-year leave to remain, and 1 event (application deadlines 23 Feb 2026 for extensions and 23 Feb 2028 for settlement). Out of scope and not recorded: other categories and general rules, Appendix KoLL language exemptions (general settlement rule).

One-page AIFC Programme Office fee table (Russian and English): administration fee excluding VAT of USD 7,750 for the main applicant only and USD 11,375 for the main applicant plus one spouse. Nothing else is printed (no fees for further family members). Earlier pass: main-applicant fee. This pass added the main-applicant-plus-spouse fee as its own rule.

AIFC document (2 pp., August 2026) listing the eligible investment instruments for the Investment Tax Residency Programme: AIX-listed securities (eligibility tests for securities and issuers: admitted to the Official List, issued by Kazakh or AIFC entities, positive trading volume on the day of purchase, not wholesale or exempt; held on an individual sub-account; replacement of matured or delisted securities), share capital of an AIFC entity (USD 60,000 minimum contribution via a local bank account, at least 3 full-time jobs for Kazakh citizens, physical office in the AIFC) and digital assets via AFSA-licensed providers (minimum per section 13 of the Regulations). The issuer and security eligibility tests contain no numbers. Earlier pass recorded nothing from this document (the ledger said the USD 60,000 was noted). This pass added 2 rules: USD 60,000 share-capital contribution and 3 jobs.

AIFC Regulations No. 42 of 2022 on the Investment Tax Residency Programme (28 pp.): eligibility (foreign national, 18+, no Kazakh tax residence or terminated citizenship in the last 20 years), application documents (bank statement within 30 days covering 3 months), due diligence, USD 60,000 minimum in one of three instrument types, Investment Resident Certificate up to 5 years, preservation, replacement (10 business days' notice), top-up and monitoring, pre-existing and earlier investments, early exit and termination, investor visa and temporary residence (family visas no longer than the investor's), tax residency and tax regime (benefits only if the tax-residence certificate fee is paid; Kazakh-source income taxed normally; family members taxed normally), interaction with state bodies, payments, definitions (family: spouse 18+, children under 18) and forms. Earlier pass: minimum investment, certificate term, launch event. This pass added 8 rules (age 18; 20-year tax-residence and citizenship exclusions; 30-day and 3-month bank statement rules; 10-business-day replacement notice; spouse 18+, children under 18), with valid_to 2026-08-05. The tax provisions contain no rates or amounts (fees are left to the Tax Code); top-up deadlines are not set here.

AIFC Regulations No. 57 of 2026 on the Investment Tax Residency Programme (31 pp.): commencement and repeal of the 2022 Regulations, Programme Office and fees (non-refundable; amounts left to the Rules), eligibility (18+, no Kazakh tax residence or terminated citizenship in the last 20 years), application documents and agents, due diligence, minimums (USD 60,000 for AIFC funds/shares, AIX securities or share capital of an AIFC Participant; USD 150,000 for digital assets; to be maintained, top-up procedure left to the Rules), certificate up to 5 years, preservation, replacement (10 business days), monitoring, early exit and termination, investor visa and residence, tax residency and tax regime, definitions (spouse 18+, children under 18) and templates. Earlier pass: the two minimums and the rule-change event. This pass added 9 rules: age 18, 20-year tax-residence and citizenship exclusions, bank statement rules (30 days, 3 months), 10-business-day replacement notice, certificate up to 5 years, spouse 18+ and children under 18. The tax provisions contain no rates or amounts.

AIFC Rules No. 5 of 2026 on the Investment Tax Residency Programme (12 pp.; approved 23 Jan 2026, in force 6 Aug 2026): Programme Office, due diligence, Programme Committee, complaints (acknowledged within 10 business days, response within 21), forms, agents (eligibility criteria without numbers), fees (at least USD 8,990 including taxes), instrument requirements (AIX securities: eligibility tests without numeric thresholds; share capital: USD 60,000, 3 jobs, AIFC office, operations within 12 months; digital assets), maintaining the minimum and top-up notice within 30 calendar days, grounds for immediate termination, definitions (spouse 18+, children under 18). Earlier pass: USD 8,990 fee and 3-jobs rule. This pass added 7 rules: USD 60,000 share-capital minimum, 12-month operations deadline, 30-day top-up/replacement notice, complaint deadlines (10 and 21 business days), spouse 18+ and children under 18.

Kazakh Government Rules on entry and stay of immigrants and on migration control (Resolution No. 148 of 21 Jan 2012, consolidated to 25 Aug 2025, with amendment footnotes): visa-free stays, registration, temporary residence permits by purpose (workers, AIFC staff, AIFC investment residents, students, family reunification, medical, business immigrants, missionaries, trafficking victims), visa issuance by internal affairs bodies (business visas up to 30 days, investor visas up to 90 days, AIFC investment-resident investor visas up to five years), EAEU workers, exit and migration control. This pass added 4 rules (AIFC investment residents' residence permit one year renewable to five years; investor visa up to five years; general investor visa up to 90 days as a context row) and 1 event (para 19-1 added by Resolution No. 140 of 17 Mar 2021). Out of scope and not recorded: other immigrant categories, business immigrants (they must run a business; decision 15), registration and migration-control rules.

Maldives Corporate Resident Visa Regulation 2021/R-115 (Dhivehi, 17 pp. with English forms): purpose and scope, three routes (foreign-investment company route under art. 5; USD 250,000 five-year fixed deposit, art. 6; USD 250,000 in government-designated businesses, art. 7), applicant age 18, application and completeness (passport valid at least 6 months), 14-day decision and 14-day visa application, passport changes within 7 days, five-year visa, renewal 90 days before expiry, cancellation, fee MVR 750 per 3 months (MVR 15,000), disclosure every three months, entry into force, definitions (family: parents, spouse, children, grandparents, grandchildren, as certified; no ages), application and declaration forms. Earlier pass: deposit and designated-investment amounts, validity, MVR 15,000 fee, entry-into-force event. This pass added 9 rules: age 18, five-year deposit term, passport validity 6 months, 14-day decision and visa-application deadlines, 7-day change notice, 90-day renewal deadline, MVR 750 per 3 months, 7-day cancellation notice. Out of scope (decision 15) and not recorded: the company-route conditions in art. 5 (50% Maldivian staff, 5 employees, USD 1 million company revenue in one of the last 3 years), which are thresholds on a company, not the applicant's investment. The family definition has no ages to record.

Rwandan Ministerial Order on nationality (Official Gazette of 25 Mar 2022, 35 pp., trilingual): documents for each ground of nationality by origin and acquisition (art. 12 for sustainable investment or activities: birth certificate, profile, residence permit, fee receipt, proof of properties, investor registration, proof of sustainable activities), application modalities, certificate contents, oath, publication, revocation, renunciation and recovery procedures, fees (FRW 5,000 by origin; FRW 10,000 by acquisition; FRW 100,000 processing; FRW 150,000 renunciation; waivers), dual-nationality declarations, commencement. This pass added 2 rules: the FRW 10,000 application fee and FRW 100,000 processing fee for nationality by acquisition, which apply to the investment ground. Out of scope and not recorded: fees and deadlines for nationality by origin, renunciation, recovery and dual-nationality declarations (not the investment route).

Rwanda's Organic Law on nationality (No. 002/2021.OL, Official Gazette of 28 Jul 2021, 45 pp., trilingual): definitions (majority 18), nationality by origin, acquisition grounds (marriage after 5 years, adoption, national interest, honour, substantial sustainable investment or activities (art. 15, no amount or residence period), residence of 15 years, special skills, immigrants after 25 years, statelessness), powers, publication, oath, certificate within 60 days, rights, revocation, renunciation and recovery, application validity of 3 years, dual nationality (declaration within 3 months), offences and penalties, repeal of the 2008 law, commencement. Earlier pass: art. 15 investment ground (amount unset) and the launch event. This pass added 6 rules: certificate within 60 days and 3-year application validity (apply to investment grants), and as context rows without a programme the 15-year residence and 25-year immigrant periods, the 5-year marriage period and the art. 50 penalty for fraudulent acquisition (FRW 3-5 million). Out of scope and not recorded: renunciation, recovery, dual-nationality procedures and the other offences (not the investment route).

Coordinated text of San Marino Law 118/2010 on entry and stay of foreigners, updated to 3 June 2025 (121 pp.), with amendment footnotes: entry, stay permits (work, study, family, humanitarian), residence (art. 16: ordinary grounds, investors in business with job commitments (art. 16(3)(c), no amount), family extension with children up to 25 (3-bis), consolidation after 10 years, health insurance EUR 30,000 for the first 24 months (3-quater)), elective residence (art. 16-bis: EUR 500,000 property or EUR 600,000 ten-year deposit, fees, cap, consolidation), atypical residence with a 7% substitute tax on foreign income (16-ter), atypical residence for pensioners (16-quater: income EUR 120,000 and EUR 300,000 movable assets held in San Marino banks since 2025; 6% / 3% substitute tax; cap 249 a year), provisional permits (16-quinquies), refusal and revocation (art. 17), expulsion, offences, and later amending laws and decrees. Earlier pass: 9 art. 16-bis rules and 2 events. This pass added 9 rules applying to elective residence: 5-year residence history, 60-day decision, 8% property registration tax, 3-month investment deadline, 24-month completion certificate, secondary-applicant children up to 25, 6-month provisional permit, and the art. 17 refusal tests (offences over one year; expulsion or revocation within ten years). Out of scope and not recorded: the business-investor residence of art. 16(3)(c) (requires running a business with job commitments and has no minimum; decision 15), the art. 16(3-quater) insurance cover (applies to art. 16(3) and 3-bis residents; elective residents must instead carry private insurance with no amount, art. 16-bis(8)(c)), arts. 16-ter (foreign-income tax regime) and 16-quater (pensioners; income-based, decision 15, see the human-decision note), ordinary stay permits and other general rules.

Turkey's Implementing Regulation of the Law on Foreigners and International Protection (RG 17 Mar 2016, current consolidated text, 27 pp.): entry, visas, residence permits (application procedure: 30-day cure period, 90-day decision, permit 60 days shorter than the passport, health insurance, sufficient means at the net minimum wage), short-term residence (one year per grant; property owners must own a dwelling used as such, co-owning family members may apply, art. 28(3); refusal after more than 120 days abroad in the last year), family, student, long-term (8 years' uninterrupted residence with absence limits), humanitarian and trafficking-victim permits, work permits, deportation, international protection. Earlier pass: the art. 28(3) property-owner condition (no amount). This pass added 9 rules that apply to the property-owner residence: one-year permits, 120-day absence limit, 90-day decision, 30-day cure period, 60-day passport margin, and long-term residence after 8 years with its absence limits (180 days a year, 365 days in 5 years, 6 months at once). Out of scope and not recorded: other permit types, international protection, deportation and visa rules. The investment ground for short-term residence and the property value thresholds are not in this regulation (they are in Law 6458 and other texts).

Uzbek Presidential Decree PF-67 of 18 Apr 2025 (lex.uz, consolidated with later amendment notes) on stimulating production, exports and business: competition in the domestic market, certification and technical regulation, customs and tax administration, production costs, export expansion (export duties, trade houses abroad up to USD 50,000 a year), investment promotion (para 26: from 1 June 2025 a 5-year residence permit in a simplified procedure for payments of USD 250,000 plus USD 150,000 per family member: spouse, child, parents), control and execution (in force immediately, para 29), and annexed lists of goods removed from mandatory certification and inspection. Para 26 is the only provision on residence or foreigners; it was fully recorded by the earlier pass (3 rules, 2 events). This pass read the whole decree and found nothing else in scope: the other sections are trade, customs, export and industry measures unrelated to the residence programme. No rows added.
